title.narrative: 17-HEKS – Organic hazelnut value chain creates income and decent employment in Western Georgia

description.narrative: Sustainable hazelnut production and transparent and profitable marketing channels reduce poverty through creating stable income and decent employment opportunities for Georgian farmer families.

The overall objective of the project is that sustainable hazelnut production and transparent and profitable value chains create income and decent employment opportunities for Georgian farmer families. The project aims to enable a significant and growing number of farmer families in Georgia to improve their liveli-hoods in a sustainable way by adopting organic and fair-trade hazelnut production practices and by enabling them to sell their produce profitably via traceable and reliable value chains. To achieve this, the project will enhance efficiency of producer cooperatives, connect them with the buyer and the PSSPs as well as contribute to positive changes in the business enabling environment using MSD methodology and thereby also enhance the economic viability of the actors in the value chain. The clear business orientation of the project has to ensure sustainability of the results beyond the project implementation.
Starting from 2022, in the framework of the new Greening Component, the Project, under the principles of market system development approach, started to further amplify and emphasize innovative, eco-friendly, effective organic agricultural practices backed by theoretical knowledge transfer, as well as practical implementation guidance and support through introduction of 4 modules like compost production, vermin-compost production, demo farmers & farmers trainings and biochar production & traceability app development.
The Danida Market Development Partnerships programme (DMDP) is designed to support commercially oriented partnerships for sustainable market development in developing countries. In addition to reporting on individually determined outputs and outcomes, all DMDP projects report on five key programme indicators. These five indicators are the same for the whole project portfolio, enabling strategic and programme level monitoring, and aggregation of results.
